---
title: Measure a source with a sky annulus
description: Use astroapers geometry and astroimred photometry on a synthetic source.
---

Construct the source aperture and background annulus in image coordinates,
then pass them to `apphot_annulus`. This example uses a synthetic Gaussian
source with a constant background.

## 1. Define the image and apertures

```{python}
import astroapers as aap
import numpy as np
from astropy.nddata import CCDData
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

from astroimred.phot.apphot import apphot_annulus

y, x = np.mgrid[:33, :33]
data = 50.0 + 500.0 * np.exp(-((x - 16) ** 2 + (y - 16) ** 2) / (2 * 1.5**2))
ccd = CCDData(data, unit="adu")
aperture = aap.CircAp((16, 16), r=4)
annulus = aap.CircAn((16, 16), r_in=7, r_out=10)
```

Positions are `(x, y)` pixel centers. The aperture radius determines which
source light contributes; the annulus estimates the local sky.

## 2. Measure background-subtracted flux

```{python}
photometry = apphot_annulus(
    ccd,
    aperture,
    annulus,
    gain=1.5,
    rdnoise=3.0,
    t_exposure=30.0,
)
assert np.all(photometry["srcsum"] > 0)
photometry[["srcsum", "mag"]]
```

The supplied gain is in electrons per ADU, read noise is in electrons, and
exposure time is in seconds. `mag` is an instrumental magnitude; no calibrated
photometric zero point is supplied in this example.

## 3. Inspect the geometry

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Synthetic source with a circular aperture and a surrounding sky annulus."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
image = ax.imshow(data, origin="lower", cmap="gray")
aperture.plot(ax=ax, color="tab:orange")
annulus.plot(ax=ax, color="tab:blue")
ax.set(xlabel="x [pixel]", ylabel="y [pixel]")
fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, label="Signal [ADU]")
plt.show()
```

For masks, error arrays, multiple sources, and return columns, use the
[`apphot_annulus` reference](../api/phot.apphot.apphot_annulus.qmd).
See [astroapers tutorials](https://ysbach.github.io/astroapers/) for alternate
aperture shapes and reusable weights.
